title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). We have a set of points P. To each 'object' X is attached a subset |X| ⊂ P and an ordered set X̃ of sub-objects Y ≤ X (with X ∈ X̃). The 'open part' is defined as |Y|° = |Y| \ ⋃_{Z<Y} |Z|. The axioms in play are:
- (i) every |Y|° is non-empty;
- (iii) the |Y|° are pairwise disjoint for distinct Y;
- (ii bis) |Y| = ⋃_{Z∈Ỹ} |Z|° (the closed piece is the union of the open strata below it);
- (ii ter) |X| = ⋃_{Y∈X̃} |Y|°.

The previous page asks whether the abstract order on X̃ is recovered from inclusion of supports: |Y| ⊂ |Z| ⇒ Y ≤ Z? It introduces L = Ỹ∩Z̃ and M = Ỹ∪Z̃.

This page proves it.
1. By (i) and (iii), the |T|° (T∈M) are non-empty and pairwise disjoint.
2. By (ii bis) for Y: |Y| = ⋃_{T∈Ỹ}|T|° = (⋃_{T∈L}|T|°) ∪ (⋃_{T∈Ỹ\L}|T|°).
3. By (ii bis) for Z: |Z| = ⋃_{T∈Z̃}|T|° contains ⋃_{T∈L}|T|°. It is disjoint from |T|° for T∈Ỹ\L, since such T are not in Z̃ and open strata are disjoint.
4. Hence |Y|∩|Z| = ⋃_{T∈L}|T|°.
5. So |Y| ⊂ |Z| iff ⋃_{T∈Ỹ\L}|T|° = ∅. Since each |T|° is non-empty, this holds iff Ỹ\L = ∅, i.e. Ỹ ⊂ Z̃. In particular Y ∈ Z̃, i.e. Y ≤ Z. 'On gagne !'

The left margin notes that (ii bis) is used not only for X but also for Y and Z.

Consequence: (ii bis), for X and all Y∈X̃, gives (ii ter): |X| is partitioned by the |Y|°, Y∈X̃. By (i) and (iii) this partition is injectively indexed by X̃: Y≠Z ⇒ |Y|°∩|Z|° = ∅, hence |Y|° ≠ |Z|° because both are non-empty.

He then asks the converse: does (ii ter) imply (ii bis)? A crossed-out reference to 'CFV p.1, Prop 1 condition 3°' follows, then an NB. The NB says the |X|° defined here agrees with the one determined by the family |Y| (Y∈X̃). Every x∈|X| lies in exactly one |Y|°, and that Y is the smallest element of X̃ with x∈|Y|. The order of X̃ is the one induced by inclusion in 𝔓(P), by the argument above.

The next page abstracts all this into a lemma. Take a poset I and a map i ↦ X_i ⊂ P, set X_i° = X_i \ ⋃_{j<i}X_j, and assume the map is increasing with X_i° non-empty and pairwise disjoint. Then the frontier-type condition X_i = ⋃_{j≤i}X_j° is equivalent to a condition on the image, and it implies that φ is an order isomorphism onto its image ordered by inclusion.

Purpose: this is the combinatorial foundation for a notion of 'stratified' object (a space or multiplicity with a poset of closed strata) in the fourth draft of Analysis situs. The order on strata must be intrinsic, namely inclusion of closures, and the open strata must partition the space.
errors: Notational slips: in the displayed unions the summation variable is written Z while the summand is |T|° (should read T∈Ỹ, T∈L, etc.).
The transcription has '⋃_{Ỹ\L}|Z|° ≠ ∅ i.e. Ỹ\L = ∅'. Mathematically the condition must be '= ∅' (|Y|⊂|Z| iff the extra union is empty). Either a slip of the pen or a misreading.
Minor gap, recognised by Grothendieck in the margin: the argument needs (ii bis) for Y and Z as well, not only for X. So the hypothesis must hold hereditarily on X̃.

The step '|Z| is disjoint from |T|° for T∈Ỹ\L' uses (ii bis) for Z together with disjointness of open strata across Ỹ∪Z̃. This needs Ỹ and Z̃ to be compatible subsets of the single ordered set X̃, which is implicit.

ideas.what: Recovering the abstract order on the index poset of strata from inclusion of closed strata, given non-empty, pairwise disjoint open strata and the condition that each closed stratum is the union of the open strata below it.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified set satisfying the frontier condition; the order on strata is the closure (specialization) order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom/Mather (frontier condition); poset-stratified spaces in modern form, e.g. Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6) discusses 'tame' stratified spaces programmatically, but not this lemma

ideas.what: Equivalence/implication between 'closure = union of lower open strata' (ii bis) and 'the space is the disjoint union of the open strata indexed by the poset' (ii ter), abstracted on the next page as a lemma about maps I → 𝔓(P).
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a set indexed by a poset, with the order recovered by inclusion of closures (order isomorphism onto the image in 𝔓(P))

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary set-theoretic bookkeeping for poset-indexed stratifications. The result (the order on strata coincides with inclusion of closures under the frontier condition) is standard and routine. Its interest is only as documentation of how the 1986 Analysis situs draft axiomatised strata.
transcription_corrections: Summation indices: '⋃_{Z∈Ỹ}|T|°', '⋃_{Z∈L}|T|°', '⋃_{Z∈Ỹ\L}|T|°' should read with T as the index (T∈Ỹ, T∈L, T∈Ỹ\L).
'q.e.d. : |Y| fermé[?] i.e. |Y|⊂|Z|' — more plausibly 'i.e. : |Y| ⊂ |Z| ssi ...' (an equivalence), not 'fermé'.
'⋃_{Z∈Ỹ\L}|Z|° ≠ ∅' should be '= ∅' to match the argument and the following 'i.e. Ỹ\L = ∅'.
Line after 'Ainsi, on a': the image reads roughly 'Ainsi, on a (pour X et les Y∈X̃) [crossed: ...] (ii bis) ⇒ (ii ter)'; the inserted '(pour X et les Y∈X̃)' replaces a crossed-out phrase.
'∃ un unique[?] et un plus petit Y∈X̃' probably reads '∃ un et un seul, et (c'est) le plus petit, Y∈X̃ avec x∈|Y|' (the x∈|Y|° vs x∈|Y| distinction matters).
